air-service-boys-in-the-big-battle-or-si: Charles Amory Beach sends his young American aviators into the great battles of the Western Front in this World War I adventure. Daring flights, dogfights with German aces, and a mission to silence the enemy's big guns keep the heroes aloft and in peril. Written while the war still raged, it thrilled boys with the newest, most romantic branch of service.
a-treatise-on-the-six-nation-indians: J. B. Mackenzie's study tells of the Six Nations, the great Iroquois league of Mohawks, Oneidas, Onondagas, Cayugas, Senecas, and Tuscaroras. He writes of their customs, their councils, and how this strong union of tribes held together long before white settlers came. A useful early record of one of North America's great native alliances.
the-loss-of-the-s-s-titanic-its-story-an: Lawrence Beesley, a second-class passenger who survived the Titanic's sinking, wrote this clear-eyed account within months of the disaster. He describes the collision, the lifeboats, and the rescue with calm precision — and draws lessons about arrogance and unpreparedness. One of the most important firsthand records of the night the great ship went down.
missionary-work-among-the-ojebway-indian: Edward Francis Wilson recounts his missionary labors among the Ojibway of the Great Lakes — their language, customs, and conversion, recorded with sympathy and care. His detailed account preserves much about nineteenth-century Indigenous life. An important and humane record. His affection for the Ojibway people shines through every chapter.
graded-lessons-in-english-an-elementary-: Reed and Kellogg's graded lessons taught generations of American schoolchildren to diagram sentences and master English grammar. One hundred practical lessons built solid foundations, sentence by sentence. The classic American grammar that shaped how the nation learned to write well.
discipline-and-other-sermons: Charles Kingsley preaches on discipline — of body, mind, and soul — in these manly, stirring sermons. His muscular Christianity speaks plainly to duty and self-rule. Vigorous Victorian faith at its best. On work, on purity, on courage in daily life, he speaks straight to the conscience of his hearers.
early-plays-catiline-the-warrior-s-barro: Henrik Ibsen's early plays — Catiline, The Warrior's Barrow, and Olaf Liljekrans — show the young dramatist finding his voice. Romantic verse dramas before the great realistic plays, they reveal the roots of his genius. Essential for Ibsen students. The future master of the modern stage is already visible in these youthful works.
a-shepherd-s-life-impressions-of-the-sou: W. H. Hudson's Shepherd's Life preserves old Caleb Bawcombe and the vanishing world of the Wiltshire downs — a shepherd's year in loving detail. His record of rural England is now an elegy and a classic. Nature writing at its most humane.
keith-of-the-border-a-tale-of-the-plains: Randall Parrish's Keith of the Border is a tale of the plains — a scout's adventures through Indian wars and frontier perils. His hero's courage and honor never waver in the face of danger. Love and loyalty lighten the trail. A stirring Western romance in the classic manner.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-leri: This entry treats Lérins, the island abbey off Cannes. Honoratus founded it in the fifth century. Jean Besse sings its island praise. Saints have prayed there for sixteen hundred years. Vincent's Commonitory was written on its sunny shore. Two saints named Honoratus made it holy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: This piece covers St. Albans, the English abbey of the first martyr. Alban's blood hallowed the Hertfordshire hill. Gilbert Huddleston gives its long history. A premier abbey of England. Matthew Paris chronicled England's kings within its walls. Its shrine drew pilgrims from every shire.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abecedarians: This 1913 reference article on the Abecedarians — the sect that scorned all book learning. John Joseph A'Becket tells their strange story. They burned books and shunned schools. Fanaticism's war on the alphabet. Luther himself argued against their book-burning zeal. Their hatred of letters died with the sect itself.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-janss: This 1913 reference article on Abraham Janssens — the Flemish painter of grand baroque scenes. George Williamson surveys his canvases. Antwerp's churches still show his work. A solid master of the Counter-Reformation. His Day and Night hang in the Vienna gallery.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acclamation-i: A 1913 entry on acclamation in papal elections — choosing a pope by sudden unanimous shout. William Fanning notes its rare use. The Spirit moves the cardinals as one. Rome's most dramatic elections. Gregory VII was hailed by the Roman crowd. Such moments were rare and momentous.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acts-of-roman: This 1913 reference article on the acts of the Roman Congregations — decrees of the Vatican's high courts. Hector Papi explains their force and form. Cardinals judged the Church's causes. Rome's tribunals, and their written word.
